text:
Riley: opened a PR to add two new SDK examples (Ruby + Rust) for audit exports and to clarify legal-hold behavior. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1417
Kai: nice. are we documenting how exports interact with tenant TTL vs legal hold? reviewers keep asking that.
Riley: yes — added a short FAQ bullet: `Exports follow tenant (customer-owned namespace) retention settings by default; a legal hold explicitly preserves records beyond TTL until release.`
Mara: can you paste the Ruby and Rust snippets here? easier to sanity-check before legal reads.
Riley: Ruby example:
```ruby
require 'redwood'
client = Redwood::Audit.new(api_key: ENV['REDWOOD_KEY'])
client.export_evidence(tenant_id: 'acme-inc', pseudonymize: true, time_window: {from: '2025-07-01', to: '2025-07-31'})
```
Rust example (using the async client):
```rust
use redwood::AuditClient;
let client = AuditClient::new(std::env::var("REDWOOD_KEY").unwrap());
client.export_evidence("acme-inc", true, ("2025-07-01", "2025-07-31")).await?;
```
Riley: sample export JSON in the doc shows fields `pseudonymized_subject_id`, `event_ts`, `action`, `resource`. I intentionally used `pseudonymized_subject_id` to avoid the repeated `user_id` token.
Kai: small ask — can we explicitly state the pseudonymization method at a high level? SOC2 reviewers liked knowing it's irreversible and tenant-salted HMAC in our earlier audit. e.g., "irreversible hashing with tenant-specific salt" (no raw algorithm details).
Mara: legal will want plain wording. pinging @legal-ops for a short approved sentence.
legal-ops: quick read 4: prefer: "Identifiers in exports are pseudonymized using an irreversible, tenant-specific HMAC; timestamps and audit metadata are retained for evidentiary purposes." avoid words like "salt" alone, but "tenant-specific HMAC" is fine. Also request we add a one-line note about keys: "Pseudonymization keys are managed per-tenant and rotated per our KMS policy."
Riley: will swap phrasing. i also added an ops note about export storage: by default exports are streamed to a KMS-encrypted presigned S3 URL; legal-hold exports require additional approvals and are stored in a locked bucket until release.
ops-oncall: adding ops note 4: ensure the runbook lists the approval flow (security + legal) and that exports for legal hold use server-side SSE-KMS and are only accessible via short-lived principals. i'll attach runbook excerpt to the PR.
Kai: can we include the exact exported field list in a tiny table so integrators can map? e.g., original -> exported: `subject.id` -> `pseudonymized_subject_id`, `email` -> `pseudonymized_email`, `session_id` -> `pseudonymized_session_id`.
Riley: added the table and a short example of downstream mapping showing hashed fields and `event_ts` preserved.
devex-bot: Reminder: docs PR checklist 5 5 add CODEOWNERS, include snippet tests (ruby + rust), run link-checker, update changelog, and add an entry to the migrations guide.
Mara: tiny nit: change every ambiguous use of "tenant" to "tenant (customer-owned namespace)" in the evidence docs to avoid SOC2 confusion.
legal-ops: approved the updated sentence and the key-management line. one more ask: replace the word "streamed" with "exported to a presigned S3 object over TLS" in the storage sentence for clarity.
Riley: done. changed wording to: "Exports are uploaded to a presigned S3 object over TLS and encrypted with SSE-KMS by default."
Kai: LGTM. i'll do a quick tech review for the SDK samples (param names + error handling) after you push the final commit.
Riley: will push in ~20m. thx all :rocket:
